Attach LOSS/HOSS (and optionally cut scores) to a data frame

Source: R/spec_helpers.R
join_score_bounds.Rd

The single supported way to bring scale-score bounds from an assessment_spec onto data. Span-tested subjects are matched on SUBJECT + GRADE; EOC subjects (those declared grades = NULL) are matched on SUBJECT alone.

Usage

join_score_bounds(data, assessment_spec, cuts = FALSE, warn_unmatched = TRUE)

Arguments

data

A data frame with SUBJECT and GRADE columns. Works on student-level data and on already-summarized tables alike.

assessment_spec

Named list describing the assessment program.

cuts

Logical. When TRUE, also attach a CUTS list-column. Default FALSE.

warn_unmatched

Logical. When TRUE (default), raise a single warning naming each SUBJECT/GRADE cell present in data that has no entry in the spec, with its row count. Set FALSE in downstream callers so one run warns once.

Value

data with GRADE coerced to integer and LOSS, HOSS (and CUTS, when requested) attached. Cells with no spec entry get NA.

Details

The EOC rule matters: states routinely report a real tested grade on EOC records — Mississippi's Algebra I records span grades 7 through 12 — while the spec declares EOC subjects without grades. Joining on SUBJECT + GRADE silently misses every one of those rows and leaves LOSS/HOSS as NA.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
source(system.file("specs/00_MS_Assessment_Spec.R", package = "ReportR"))
dat <- join_score_bounds(student_results_long, assessment_spec)
} # }
